figures.caption: Figure 1: Hierarchical Causal Entanglement. Bottom (Micro-Latent): Only the red subset {tic} causally drives Y ; the blue subset {tjnc} contains spurious factors correlated with Z. Middle (MesoLatent): Micro-variables abstract into causal (TC) and non-causal (TnC) clusters. Top (Observed): We observe only the entangled treatment T = m(TC , TnC), which creates the spurious backdoor path T ← TnC ← Z → Y that standard models will exploit.

Figure 3: Synthetic SCM, sweep over outcome-noise scale σY ∈ [0, 1] across 2,000 seeds per noise level. Lines are per-seed medians; shaded bands are the inter-quartile range across seeds. Left: intervention sensitivity |Ŷ (T )− Ŷ (T ′)|, where T ′ resamples the non-causal coordinates of T ; lower is better, with 0 indicating that the model has not absorbed any signal from TnC . Right: paired ∆MAE = MAECRL −MAEbaseline per seed, centred on the zero line. The CRL penalty does not degrade predictive performance, and is in fact slightly better at higher noise levels.

Figure 4: Progressive removal of non-causal leakage. The objective J(g) is plotted as a function of the penalty weight λ for representations retaining different amounts of the non-causal component TnC . Since TnC contributes confounder information without adding outcome information beyond TC , representations with more non-causal leakage incur a larger penalty. The purely causal representation g(T ) = TC achieves the highest score among the tested representations.

Figure 5: Lossless regime and critical penalty weight. The objective J(g) is plotted as a function of λ for stochastic compressed representations G = TC + ϵG, where ϵG ∼ N (0, σ2 G). The dashed curve corresponds to the uncompressed causal representation σ2 G = 0. For small λ, preserving the full causal component is optimal; for larger λ, compression can become preferable because the reduction in confounder information outweighs the utility loss.
